item.title: AI fever ignites a boom in thematic ETFs as fund managers hunt for their next big hit
item.dc:creator: World Stock News Editorial Desk
item.description: The runaway success of the artificial-intelligence trade has left investors hungry for the next big market theme. Wall Street fund managers are happily obliging with a flurry of new targeted products, helping investors invest in everything ...

item.title: My husband wants to sell our $1.5 million home and invest the proceeds. But this is where we raised our kids — and I can’t bear to leave.
item.dc:creator: World Stock News Editorial Desk
item.description: “He wants to buy something for $600,000 now that we are empty-nesters.”

item.title: ‘Non-answers’ aren’t working. This is what investors really need from the Fed.
item.dc:creator: World Stock News Editorial Desk
item.description: What really matters to investors, economists say, is for Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh to prove he can successfully communicate the central bank’s strategy.

item.title: Do machines have feelings? AI has philosophers and tech leaders rethinking consciousness.
item.dc:creator: World Stock News Editorial Desk

item.title: This hot AI-fueled stock has been in a rut. It just beat earnings expectations by 36%.
item.dc:creator: World Stock News Editorial Desk
item.description: A company beating earnings expectations by 36% and revenue expectations by 15% would usually see a postresults bump. But not for Bloom Energy, the fuel-cell maker that has flourished due to data-center demand.

item.title: The U.S. economy is great by this measure, and the good times aren’t over. So why are Americans so sour?
item.dc:creator: World Stock News Editorial Desk
item.description: A once-in-a-generation investment boom has created lots of winners — but many Americans are feeling left out.

item.title: Oil markets are on edge ahead of the weekend, as midterm elections near and fresh U.S. strikes on Iran are predicted
item.dc:creator: World Stock News Editorial Desk
item.description: Oil has climbed back to an Iran-war high and may soon go higher, if the U.S. and Israel strike Iran after their respective voters go to the polls in the coming days.
